newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TO ALLOW COMPANIES TO OWN FARMLAND.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TO ALLOW COMPANIES TO OWN FARMLAND.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Thursday unveiled a new bill approved by the government allowing the purchase of farmland by Hungarian-registered companies regardless of the nationality of their owners.

Horn told a news conference following the cabinet's meeting that the government approved the first draft of an amendment of the law on farmland, and the ministers agreed that Hungary should open the way for companies to buy land.
"By this move we can strengthen the activities of (agricultural) cooperatives and companies," he said.
He denied allegations by opposition parties that the government planned to allow direct land sales to foreigners.
However, domestic companies owned by foreigners will be allowed to buy farmland, added Elemer Kiss, Secretary of State for the Prime Minister's Office added.
"It is not question who the (company) owner is -- the owner will only hold a stake in a company (and not the land)," he said.
He said Hungary would not allow direct sales of farmland to foreigners because prices on Hungary's illiquid farmland markets were much lower than in western countries.
"Government protection on farmland is necessary so as to not let foreigners buy it up," he said.

He added that the law amendment is likely to boost the market and help the concentration of farmland, which had been fragmented by compensation to smallholders who lost their land after World War Two under the country's communist regime.
Horn said that in the opinion of government experts the law amendment meets the requirements of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
However, before finalising the draft law amendment, the government will consult with experts and the representatives of farmers and the opposition, Horn said.
These talks should be closed by June 30, he said.
